course_name_original: Sistemas Fotovoltaicos y Eólicos de Producción de Energía Eléctrica
course_name_en: Photovoltaic and Wind Power Generation Systems

learning_outcomes.text: Assess the importance of renewable energies in the current energy and environmental scenario.
Design grid-connected photovoltaic systems and isolated photovoltaic systems.
Identify the main elements that are part of a wind turbine and its control systems, relating them to the task they perform.
Relate the constructive and technical characteristics of the electrical systems that are part of a wind turbine to the power provided for different wind speeds.
Describe the structure and operation of wind power generation systems based on doubly fed induction generators.

syllabus_topics: Situation of PV generation in Spain and in the World.
Selection criteria for a solar panel.
Calculation of peak sun hours for a location.
Control of active and reactive power flows.
Sizing of wiring for a solar installation.
Selection of protection and switching equipment in the DC circuit of the solar generator: fuses, switches, overvoltage protection and insulation monitors.
Selection of protection and switching equipment in the AC circuit of the solar plant: automatic switch for interconnection, automatic switch, differential protection and overvoltage protection.
Sizing of a grid-connected solar plant.
Simulation of a grid-connected solar plant.
Sizing of an isolated photovoltaic system.
Autonomy time of an isolated photovoltaic system.
Current status of wind energy in Spain and in the World.
Wind turbines based on synchronous and asynchronous generators.
WIND TURBINES EQUIPPED WITH A DOUBLY FED INDUCTION GENERATOR
Control of a wind turbine equipped with a doubly fed induction generator.
Analysis of active and reactive power flows through the stator and through the back-to-back converter.
Management of reactive power flows in a wind farm.
The synchronous generator in direct-drive wind turbines.
The multipolar synchronous generator in wind turbines.
Practice Session 1- Calculation of solar production of a photovoltaic plant.
Practice Session 2- Analysis and simulation of a photovoltaic solar generator.
Practice Session 3- Simulation of the connection of a PV plant to the distribution grid.
Practice Session 4- Monitoring of the equipment that is part of a FV solar plant.
Practice Session 5- Monitoring of a grid-connected doubly fed wind turbine.
Practice Session 6- Active and reactive power control in a DFIG wind turbine.
Practice Session 7- Automatic operation of a doubly fed wind turbine.

assessment_methods.method: Practical assignment (TRB) - Sizing and simulation of a Photovoltaic Solar Plant

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment (January call), the final grade is calculated as 0.8*EXF + 0.1*TRB + 0.1*(0.6*GUILAB + 0.4*FINLAB), provided that EXF >= 5 and (0.6*GUILAB + 0.4*FINLAB) >= 5. Otherwise, the final grade is 'Fail'. The partial exam note is only considered for that block in the final exam, and neither the partial exam note nor the TRB grade are considered in extraordinary evaluations. For single evaluation (May and July calls), the final grade is 0.9*EXF + 0.1*(LAB), provided that EXF >= 5 and LAB >= 5, where LAB is evaluated in a complementary test. Otherwise, the final grade is 'Fail'. Students under differentiated evaluation will have a single test covering theory, classroom practices, and laboratory practices, without partial exams or assignments.
